title: Mean Flows for One-step Generative Modeling

nodes.text: MeanFlow is a one-step generative modeling framework that introduces the notion of average velocity (displacement over a time interval) to characterize flow fields, in contrast to the instantaneous velocity modeled by Flow Matching.
nodes.evidence: We introduce the notion of average velocity to characterize flow fields, in contrast to instantaneous velocity modeled by Flow Matching methods.

nodes.text: The MeanFlow Identity, u(zt,r,t) = v(zt,t) - (t-r) d/dt u(zt,r,t), is derived purely from the definition of average velocity and used as a regression target to train a network to model average velocity.
nodes.evidence: We refer to this equation as the 'MeanFlow Identity', which describes the relation between v and u.

nodes.text: MeanFlow is self-contained and requires no pre-training, distillation, or curriculum learning, unlike distillation-based and curriculum-dependent one-step approaches.
nodes.evidence: Our method ... is self-contained and requires no pre-training, distillation, or curriculum learning.

nodes.text: Unlike Consistency Models, which impose a consistency constraint on network behavior with the underlying ground-truth field unknown, MeanFlow's identity derives from a ground-truth average-velocity field independent of any neural network.
nodes.evidence: the consistency constraint is imposed as a property of the network's behavior, while the properties of the underlying ground-truth field that should guide learning remain unknown

nodes.text: MeanFlow generalizes Flow Matching: restricting the formulation to t = r makes the extra time-derivative term vanish, recovering standard Flow Matching exactly.
nodes.evidence: if we were to restrict to the condition t = r, then the second term vanishes, and the method would exactly match standard Flow Matching.

nodes.text: Consistency Models fix r=0 and are conditioned on a single time variable, whereas Shortcut and IMM models add two-time self-consistency constraints; MeanFlow is conditioned on two time variables but is driven solely by the average-velocity definition with no extra constraint.
nodes.evidence: Consistency Models ... corresponds to fixing r = 0 for any t ... the Shortcut [13] and IMM [52] models ... introduce additional two-time self-consistency constraints. In contrast, our method is solely driven by the definition of average velocity

nodes.text: The Flow Map of Boffi et al. corresponds to displacement (integral of the flow between two steps), whereas MeanFlow is based on average velocity.
nodes.evidence: In comparison to the average velocity our method is based on, the Flow Map corresponds to displacement.

nodes.text: MeanFlow achieves an FID of 3.43 with a single function evaluation (1-NFE) on ImageNet 256x256 trained from scratch, outperforming previous state-of-the-art one-step diffusion/flow models by a relative margin of 50% to 70%.
nodes.evidence: it achieves an FID of 3.43 with a single function evaluation (1-NFE) on ImageNet 256x256 trained from scratch ... a relative margin of 50% to 70%

nodes.text: MeanFlow substantially narrows the gap between one-step diffusion/flow models and their multi-step predecessors.
nodes.evidence: Our study substantially narrows the gap between one-step diffusion/flow models and their multi-step predecessors

nodes.text: The time-derivative term in the MeanFlow Identity is computed as a Jacobian-vector product between the Jacobian of u and the tangent vector [v, 0, 1], efficiently evaluated via the jvp interface (torch.func.jvp or jax.jvp) in a single backward pass.
nodes.evidence: the total derivative is given by the Jacobian-vector product (JVP) between [partial_z u, partial_r u, partial_t u] ... and the tangent vector [v, 0, 1]

nodes.text: A stop-gradient is applied to the regression target to avoid double backpropagation through the JVP, eliminating higher-order optimization, with overhead under 20% of total training time in the JAX implementation.
nodes.evidence: a stop-gradient (sg) operation is applied on the target utgt ... it eliminates the need for 'double backpropagation' through the Jacobian-vector product

nodes.text: Classifier-free guidance is incorporated as a property of the underlying ground-truth field rather than applied naively at sampling, incurring no additional NFE cost when guidance is used.
nodes.evidence: we treat CFG as a property of the underlying ground-truth fields ... incurring no additional cost at sampling time when guidance is used.

nodes.text: The marginal velocity field in Flow Matching typically induces curved trajectories even when conditional flows are designed to be straight, causing coarse ODE discretization to give inaccurate results.
nodes.evidence: even when the conditional flows are designed to be straight ('rectified') ... the marginal velocity field (Eq. (1)) typically induces a curved trajectory.
